target_customer: Financial and professional service firms such as wealth managers, accountants and tax firms, private equity, insurers, mortgage lenders and family offices
problem: Firms spend staff time on repetitive document-heavy workflows. Pollen supplies an AI employee trained on each firm's own past examples and procedures.
business_model: B2B software or service, AI employee per firm with setup by the Pollen team (pricing not found)
product_category: Vertical AI agents for financial firms

founders.name: Noah Yin
founders.background_notes: Also did COVID-19 classification ML research at Columbia per the YC page.

founders.name: Aldrin Ong
education: UC Berkeley, computer science, class of 2025
founders.background_notes: Has published three apps on the App Store.

founders.name: Jeffrey Yum
founders.background_notes: Listed in the launch post, not in the YC founder profile.

competitors.name: Thomson Reuters CoCounsel agentic tax and accounting
competitors.what: Agentic AI for tax, audit and accounting professionals

competitors.name: Intapp Celeste
competitors.what: Agentic AI platform for professional firms using firm playbooks
competitors.traction_then: Announced February 2026, just after the batch started

technical_complexity.rationale: Document extraction, per-firm tuning and tests against past examples, human approval checkpoints and traceability are standard LLM engineering with some hard accuracy work.

defensibility.rationale: Per-firm training on workflows creates some lock-in, but large vendors and many startups offer similar agents.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents shipped agentic products for professional firms in 2025 and early 2026. No acquisition of Pollen found.

market_need_then: Professional firms were adopting agentic AI in 2025 and 2026, shown by launches from Thomson Reuters and Intapp; Pollen's own site cites matched-output tests but no customer count.

branding.domain_note: Original pollen.cx redirects permanently to pollen.so. Many other companies use the name Pollen.

identity.mascot_or_character: Agents are called Pollenators, with a demo agent named Paul
identity.voice_and_tone: Plain, professional, focused on audit trails and human approval

branding.brand_signature: Pollenator as the name for each AI employee

rebrands.why: Not stated; the domain redirect is the only evidence

brand_strength.rationale: Pollenator is a small memorable touch, but the name is generic and shared with several unrelated companies, and there is no brand press.

outcome_analysis: Pollen is a three-person W26 company that has narrowed from a customer-success framing in its YC launch to AI employees for financial firms. Its site says it is backed by Y Combinator and Robinhood Ventures, with no amounts or customers disclosed. It faces large incumbents, and nothing public shows traction yet, so the outcome is open.
notes: Funding: one aggregator shows $500K in one round with no investors; unverified so not recorded as a round. The company site names Y Combinator and Robinhood Ventures as backers, with no amount. The outcome search returned a different Pollen (events tech) that collapsed in 2022; it is unrelated. Competitor list is of adjacent professional-services agents, not exact matches. Completeness pass: one aggregator reports $500K in one round with no date or investors; recorded as a round resting on a single database (stage unknown). Cross-check search found no press or filing.
